genZNote: That pear-shaped trophozoite with two nuclei is basically impossible to unsee once you've learned it.

morphology.shape: Pear-shaped (teardrop) trophozoite with bilateral symmetry; oval cyst form

habitat.hostAssociation: Infects humans and various mammals; cysts are the infective, environmentally resistant stage
habitat.environmentalOccurrence: Cysts survive well in cold water, including mountain streams and municipal water supplies with inadequate treatment
habitat.reservoir: Human and animal intestinal tract; contaminated water sources

microscopy.stain: Iodine wet mount; trichrome stain of stool
microscopy.appearance: Trophozoite: pear-shaped with two nuclei giving a characteristic 'face' appearance, four pairs of flagella, and a ventral adhesive disc. Cyst: oval with 2-4 nuclei

culture.media: Not routinely cultured in clinical labs

identificationClues: Pear-shaped trophozoite with two nuclei giving a distinctive 'face' appearance
Ventral sucking disc for attachment to intestinal mucosa
Oval, multinucleated cysts on stool O&P exam
A common cause of waterborne parasitic diarrhea, including in developed countries

virulenceFactors: Ventral adhesive disc — attachment to intestinal epithelium, disrupting absorption
Variant-specific surface proteins — antigenic variation aiding immune evasion
clinicalImportance.transmission: Fecal-oral route — ingestion of cysts in contaminated water or food; also person-to-person spread in settings with limited hygiene, such as childcare centers
clinicalImportance.epidemiology: One of the most common causes of parasitic diarrheal illness worldwide, including in travelers and in outbreaks linked to contaminated recreational or drinking water
clinicalImportance.labSignificance: Stool antigen testing and PCR have largely supplemented traditional O&P microscopy for routine diagnosis due to higher sensitivity

examFacts.keyBiochemicalReaction: Not a biochemical-test organism — diagnosed by stool microscopy, antigen testing, or PCR
examFacts.importantTest: Stool antigen ELISA; trichrome-stained stool O&P exam
examFacts.distinguishingFeature: Pear-shaped trophozoite with a characteristic two-nuclei 'face' appearance and ventral sucking disc
